metadata.title: Yellow eyes and nausea in a 22-year-old after eating out
metadata.author: seed

patient.name: Sana Tariq
patient.personality: Anxious about the yellow colour of her eyes

history.chief_complaint: Yellowing of the eyes and skin with nausea for 4 days

history_of_presenting_illness.prodrome: A week of tiredness, nausea, poor appetite and a distaste for fatty/fried food
history_of_presenting_illness.jaundice: Then noticed yellow eyes, dark urine and pale stools
history_of_presenting_illness.fever: Low-grade fever early on, now settling
history_of_presenting_illness.exposure: Ate at several roadside eateries; unfiltered water; a classmate had jaundice recently

drug_history: No regular medicines, no herbal/hepatotoxic remedies

general.appearance: Visibly jaundiced (sclera and skin), not encephalopathic

abdomen.palpation: Tender, smooth hepatomegaly; no splenomegaly or ascites

general_skin.stigmata_cld: No spider naevi or palmar erythema

laboratory.name: Liver Function Tests
laboratory.result: ALT 1450, AST 1200 (markedly raised), bilirubin high, ALP mildly raised

laboratory.name: Hepatitis Viral Serology
laboratory.result: Anti-HAV IgM positive (Hep B and C negative)

laboratory.name: Coagulation Profile
laboratory.clinical_significance: Key marker of severity / acute liver failure

imaging.name: Abdominal Ultrasound
imaging.result: Mild hepatomegaly, patent vessels, no biliary obstruction or gallstones

bedside.name: Pregnancy Test
bedside.clinical_significance: Hepatitis E in pregnancy is dangerous — always check

diagnosis.explanation: A young patient with a viral prodrome, jaundice with dark urine and pale stools, tender hepatomegaly, a markedly hepatocellular LFT pattern with a normal INR, positive anti-HAV IgM and no biliary obstruction on ultrasound, has acute viral hepatitis A from faecal-oral exposure.

emergency_management: Confirm it is not acute liver failure (check INR and mental state)
Stop any hepatotoxic drugs; avoid alcohol
Monitor LFTs and INR for deterioration
definitive_management: Most hepatitis A is self-limiting; arrange outpatient follow-up
Refer urgently if signs of acute liver failure (rising INR, encephalopathy)
follow_up: Hand and food hygiene; safe water
Hepatitis A vaccination of contacts where appropriate
patient_education: It usually resolves on its own
Hygiene to prevent spread; return if drowsy or bleeding

items.description: Characterised jaundice, dark urine, pale stools
Asked about food/water exposure and contacts
Examined abdomen/liver and looked for encephalopathy
Monitor INR/mental state for acute liver failure

pearls: INR and mental state — not bilirubin — define the severity of acute hepatitis.
Always exclude pregnancy: hepatitis E carries high mortality in pregnancy.
pitfalls: Missing obstructive jaundice — ultrasound excludes a surgical cause.
Missing early acute liver failure (rising INR, drowsiness).
learning_objectives: Recognise acute liver failure and manage supportively.
